1	import { useEffect, useState } from 'react';
2	import {
3	  clearSessionJSONItem,
4	  getSessionJSONItem,
5	  setSessionJSONItem,
6	} from '@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/utils/utils';
7	
8	/**
9	 * Outcome of one wishlist-move attempt. The actual SFCC SDK calls (wishlist add + cart removal)
10	 * are the caller's own responsibility — SFCC-11 plan step 4.6 (`cartDrawerContainer.tsx`, not
11	 * built yet) — this file only reports what happened, matching the exact discriminated-union
12	 * pattern `useCartMergeAndCap.ts`'s own `CartCapResult` already established
13	 * (`overrides/app/hooks/useCartMergeAndCap.ts:25-29`), per typescript.md's stated preference for
14	 * a discriminated union over a pile of optional fields.
15	 */
16	export type WishlistMoveResult =
17	  | { status: 'success' }
18	  | { status: 'already-in-wishlist' }
19	  | { status: 'error'; error: unknown };
20	
21	/**
22	 * sessionStorage key PREFIX for "a guest asked to move THIS specific cart line to their wishlist
23	 * before authenticating." Namespaced per `productId` — see `pendingWishlistCartItemKey` below —
24	 * so that two different cart rows' pending intents can never collide in a single shared slot: a
25	 * guest beginning a pending move on row A, then row B, before either completes a redirect-based
26	 * auth flow, must leave both independently resumable rather than row B's write silently
27	 * overwriting row A's. Deliberately a distinct mechanism, and a distinct key, from
28	 * `useWishlistAuthDrawer.ts`'s own `PENDING_WISHLIST_INTENT_KEY`
29	 * (`overrides/app/hooks/useWishlistAuthDrawer.ts:43`): that key answers "which mounted drawer
30	 * instance's `onAuthSuccess` should fire after a social-IDP redirect" — its own
31	 * `PendingWishlistIntent` type carries only `intentId`/`timestamp`, no item identity at all.
32	 * This hook answers a different question — "which cart LINE was pending" — so it is a new,
33	 * separate mechanism rather than an addition to that shared type. The SFCC-11 plan explicitly
34	 * rejects adding an `itemId` field to that shared type: it has three other existing call sites
35	 * (header/rightBar, drawer-menu, product-view) and changing it is out of this step's scope.
36	 */
37	const PENDING_WISHLIST_CART_ITEM_KEY_PREFIX = 'zimmPendingWishlistCartItem';
38	
39	/**
40	 * Builds the per-product sessionStorage key — see `PENDING_WISHLIST_CART_ITEM_KEY_PREFIX`'s own
41	 * doc for why storage is namespaced this way instead of one shared key.
42	 */
43	const pendingWishlistCartItemKey = (productId: string): string =>
44	  `${PENDING_WISHLIST_CART_ITEM_KEY_PREFIX}:${productId}`;
45	
46	/**
47	 * Same 5-minute bound as `useWishlistAuthDrawer.ts`'s own `PENDING_WISHLIST_INTENT_MAX_AGE_MS`
48	 * (`overrides/app/hooks/useWishlistAuthDrawer.ts:52` — `5 * 60 * 1000`), and the same reasoning:
49	 * long enough for a real auth round trip, short enough that a long-abandoned attempt cannot
50	 * misfire later against a much later, unrelated cart session. Not imported from that file — the
51	 * constant is not exported there, and this step does not modify that file (out of scope; see the
52	 * SFCC-11 plan step 4.4's manifest and its "explicitly rejected" list). Redefined here as an
53	 * independent, same-valued constant instead.
54	 */
55	const PENDING_WISHLIST_MAX_AGE_MS = 5 * 60 * 1000; // 5 minutes
56	
57	type PendingWishlistCartItem = {
58	  /**
59	   * Matched against this row's own `productId`, not `itemId` — deliberate. A guest's basket may
60	   * be merged into a registered customer's basket between the guest's click and the shopper
61	   * completing auth (SFCC-250 step 4.1, `useWishlistAuthDrawer.ts`'s own `isRegistered` effect),
62	   * and that merge can change which `itemId` a given product line carries (it merges into a
63	   * destination basket via `createDestinationBasket: true`). `productId` is stable across that
64	   * boundary; `itemId` is not — keying the match on `itemId` would risk silently failing to
65	   * resume a legitimate pending move the moment a merge has actually happened. See this step's
66	   * own report for the related, still-open sequencing question this raises for step 4.6.
67	   */
68	  productId: string;
69	  timestamp: number;
70	};
71	
72	export type UsePendingWishlistItemParams = {
73	  /** Identifies this cart line for matching a resumed intent — see PendingWishlistCartItem's own
74	   *  doc comment for why this is `productId`, not `itemId`. */
75	  productId: string;
76	  /** Whether the current shopper is unauthenticated. Passed down from the caller (e.g. read once
77	   *  from `useCustomerType()` at the cart container) rather than read by this hook itself — see
78	   *  `zimmCartItemActions/index.tsx`'s own architecture note for why. */
79	  isGuest: boolean;
80	  /** Called (no arguments) once a previously-pending move for THIS row should be attempted.
81	   *  Fires at most once per stored intent — never for another row's pending item, never twice
82	   *  for the same one. */
83	  onResume: () => void | Promise<void>;
84	};
85	
86	export type UsePendingWishlistItemReturn = {
87	  /** Call when a guest clicks "Move to Wishlist" for this row — persists the pending intent to
88	   *  both React state (survives the email-code/create-account flows, which never unload the
89	   *  page) and session storage (survives the Apple/Google redirect, which reloads it), so
90	   *  `onResume` fires automatically once `isGuest` becomes false for this same product. */
91	  beginPendingMove: () => void;
92	};
93	
94	/**
95	 * Hook — persists a guest's "move to wishlist" intent for one cart line across an authentication
96	 * step, and resumes it once the shopper is no longer a guest. Extracted per
97	 * `.claude/rules/components.md`'s extract-to-hook threshold: this is React state plus a
98	 * non-trivial effect (session-storage read/write/clear, a 5-minute age check, resuming after a
99	 * simulated page reload) that would otherwise sit inline in `ZimmCartItemActions`.
100	 *
101	 * Deliberately calls no auth or `commerce-sdk-react` hook itself — `isGuest` arrives as a plain
102	 * prop, and the actual move (`onResume`) is the caller's own already-composed function. Only ONE
103	 * `useWishlistAuthDrawer` instance may exist for the whole cart (SFCC-11 plan step 4.4's own
104	 * explicit rejection of "one per line item"), so that real hook cannot live inside a component
105	 * that mounts once per cart line — this hook stays calling-hook-free so it can safely mount once
106	 * per row, alongside it, without reproducing that rejected shape.
107	 *
108	 * @returns `beginPendingMove`, the one function a guest click calls.
109	 */
110	export const usePendingWishlistItem = ({
111	  productId,
112	  isGuest,
113	  onResume,
114	}: UsePendingWishlistItemParams): UsePendingWishlistItemReturn => {
115	  const [pending, setPending] = useState<PendingWishlistCartItem | undefined>(undefined);
116	
117	  const beginPendingMove = () => {
118	    const intent: PendingWishlistCartItem = { productId, timestamp: Date.now() };
119	    setPending(intent);
120	    setSessionJSONItem(pendingWishlistCartItemKey(productId), intent);
121	  };
122	
123	  // Mirrors useWishlistAuthDrawer.ts's own redirect-consuming effect (that file's second
124	  // useEffect, [isRegistered]-only deps, overrides/app/hooks/useWishlistAuthDrawer.ts:252-259) —
125	  // runs on mount and on every `isGuest` change, not only on a true-to-false transition, because
126	  // a fresh mount after a real page reload (Apple/Google redirect) already has `isGuest === false`
127	  // on its very first render, with no transition to observe.
128	  useEffect(() => {
129	    if (isGuest) return;
130	
131	    const stored = getSessionJSONItem(pendingWishlistCartItemKey(productId)) as PendingWishlistCartItem | undefined;
132	    // The per-product key above already means `stored` can only ever be what THIS row itself
133	    // wrote — a different row's pending intent lives under its own, different key and is never
134	    // read, resumed, or cleared from here. This productId match is a defensive belt-and-suspenders
135	    // check on top of that (never act on foreign/malformed data even if it somehow ended up in
136	    // this slot), not the mechanism that keeps two rows apart.
137	    const mineFromStorage = stored?.productId === productId ? stored : undefined;
138	    const candidate = pending ?? mineFromStorage;
139	    if (!candidate) return;
140	
141	    // Found something of mine — clear both stores now, regardless of whether it turns out to be
142	    // fresh or stale below (a stale intent must not linger either — nothing resumes it later).
143	    // Only ever clears THIS row's own key — another row's still-pending intent, under its own
144	    // key, is untouched.
145	    setPending(undefined);
146	    clearSessionJSONItem(pendingWishlistCartItemKey(productId));
147	
148	    const isFresh = Date.now() - candidate.timestamp <= PENDING_WISHLIST_MAX_AGE_MS;
149	    if (isFresh) {
150	      void onResume();
151	    }
152	  }, [isGuest]);
153	
154	  return { beginPendingMove };
155	};

import { defineStyleConfig } from '@chakra-ui/react';

/**
 * Recipe — the "Remove" / "Move to Wishlist" action-links row (SFCC-270 AC8, SFCC-272). Single
 * style, no parts: both links get their full visual treatment from `ZimmLink`'s own recipe
 * (`zimmLink.css.ts`, size `small` — capitalize, 12px/500/14px-lh, plus that recipe's own
 * hover/focus-visible states); this recipe only owns the row's own layout, matching
 * `zimmLink/zimmLink.css.ts`'s own single-style shape rather than
 * `zimmQuantityStepper.css.ts`'s multi-part one, since there is no second visual sub-part here to
 * name.
 *
 * `gap` — Figma specifies 25px (§11.10(4) of the SFCC-11 plan); no `--zimm-scale-*` step lands on
 * 25 (foundation/spacing.ts's steps go ...m:16px, l:20px, xl:24px, 2xl:32px... — confirmed no
 * 25px entry), so this snaps to the nearest existing token, 24px (`xl`), and records the raw
 * design value here rather than typing an unregistered one-off literal.
 *
 * `color` on each link is NOT set here: `ZimmLink`'s own `link.default` alias
 * (`foundation/colour.ts:87`, `grey[900]`) and `foundation/colour.ts:61`'s `text.default` (also
 * `grey[900]`) are the same primitive, so plain `<ZimmLink>` already renders the colour this
 * component's own spec calls for — adding a second, competing colour declaration here would be
 * exactly the anti-pattern `.claude/rules/overrideStyling.md`'s "One canonical styling surface
 * per component type" section warns against (a value that can drift from the atom's own recipe
 * over time instead of there being only one place it's declared).
 */
export const ZimmCartItemActions = defineStyleConfig({
  baseStyle: {
    display: 'flex',
    alignItems: 'center',
    gap: 'var(--zimm-scale-xl)', // Figma: 25px, snapped to the nearest token (24px)
  },
});

7	
8	export const ZimmLink = defineStyleConfig({
9	  baseStyle: {
10	    display: 'inline-flex',
11	    alignItems: 'center',
12	    // WCAG 2.2 AA SC 2.5.8 — 24px minimum target. Inline text links are exempt when
13	    // the line spacing provides a 24px offset, but explicit vertical padding ensures
14	    // both sizes reliably clear the threshold. Matches Figma's container py: 4px
15	    // (alias/space/100 = var(--zimm-scale-2xs)).
16	    paddingBlock: 'var(--zimm-scale-2xs)',
17	    fontFamily: 'var(--zimm-font-family-body)',
18	    fontWeight: 'var(--zimm-font-weight-medium)',
19	    letterSpacing: 'var(--zimm-font-letterspacing-xs)',
20	    textDecoration: 'underline',

22	    border: 'none',

29	    },

1	import { defineMessages, useIntl } from 'react-intl';
2	import { useToast } from '@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/hooks/use-toast';
3	
4	/**
5	 * `@salesforce/retail-react-app` ships no TypeScript types (AGENTS.md's "Commerce SDK types not
6	 * importable" gotcha) — `use-toast.js` falls through `overrides/app/types/vendor.d.ts`'s catch-all
7	 * `declare module '@salesforce/retail-react-app/*'` (a shorthand ambient module declaration that
8	 * types the whole module `any` — see that file's own comment, and
9	 * `overrides/app/utils/recentlyViewedFullHistoryCard.ts`'s identical narrow-local-type pattern for
10	 * another untyped base function), so the real `useToast()` return value is implicitly `any`.
11	 * Declared narrow here, covering only the two fields this file actually sends (`title`, `status`)
12	 * rather than the base hook's full options surface (`description`, `action`, `position`,
13	 * `duration`, `variant`, `isClosable`) — nothing in this file uses those, so typing them would be
14	 * speculative. `status`'s four values are copied verbatim from the base hook's real accepted set
15	 * (not narrowed to only `'success' | 'warning'`), so a later message that genuinely needs `'error'`
16	 * or `'info'` — SFCC-404's rework, or any message added after this step — is already covered
17	 * without a signature change here.
18	 *
19	 * This is a type annotation documenting an assumed shape, not a runtime guarantee — TypeScript
20	 * allows asserting `any` to any narrower type with no check. The real proof is this file's own
21	 * test, which asserts the exact object the mocked toast function is called with.
22	 */
23	type CartToastStatus = 'success' | 'error' | 'info' | 'warning';
24	type CartToastFn = (options: { title: string; status: CartToastStatus }) => void;
25	
26	/**
27	 * The three real cart messages this step ships, copy verbatim from Figma (SFCC-11 plan step 4.3)
28	 * — this file never derives or paraphrases copy, only interpolates a product name into the one
29	 * message that needs it. SFCC-272's own AC text describes a generic stacked wording ("Item added
30	 * to Wishlist") for when more than one item has been added — deliberately not built here: a toast
31	 * has no aggregation concept, so that copy is only reachable once SFCC-404 ships real message
32	 * stacking. Until then every add uses this product-named variant, one toast per add.
33	 *
34	 * Wrapped in `defineMessages` (fixed 2026-09-20 — the original version of this file hardcoded
35	 * plain strings, the only visible cart copy in this build that did) so these three strings are
36	 * discoverable by whatever tooling extracts copy for this storefront's 11 locales the same way
37	 * `zimmQuantityStepper`'s own `messages` object already is. `defaultMessage` uses ICU
38	 * MessageFormat's `{productName}` placeholder syntax for the one message that interpolates.
39	 */
40	const messages = defineMessages({
41	  addedToWishlist: {
42	    id: 'use_cart_messages.added_to_wishlist',
43	    defaultMessage: '{productName} added to Wishlist',
44	  },
45	  alreadyInWishlist: {
46	    id: 'use_cart_messages.already_in_wishlist',
47	    defaultMessage: 'An item in your bag already exists in Wishlist',
48	  },
49	  maxQuantityReached: {
50	    id: 'use_cart_messages.max_quantity_reached',
51	    defaultMessage: 'An item in your bag has reached maximum quantity',
52	  },
53	});
54	
55	export type UseCartMessagesReturn = {
56	  /**
57	   * SFCC-272 AC5 — a single product was moved from the cart to the wishlist. `productName` is
58	   * interpolated into the copy on every call — never hardcode a specific product's name at a call
59	   * site. `success` status.
60	   */
61	  notifyAddedToWishlist: (productName: string) => void;
62	  /**
63	   * SFCC-272 AC6 — the item already exists in the shopper's wishlist; the caller leaves the cart
64	   * line untouched. Verbatim copy, no interpolation. `warning` status — see
65	   * `notifyMaxQuantityReached`'s own doc for why cart feedback that doesn't block anything reads
66	   * as a warning in this build, not an error.
67	   */
68	  notifyAlreadyInWishlist: () => void;
69	  /**
70	   * CAI-017 / SFCC-250 — a cart line has reached its maximum orderable quantity (the line is
71	   * already capped by `useCartMergeAndCap` before this ever fires). `warning`, not `error`:
72	   * CAI-017's own requirement text says "an error message will be displayed", but the Figma
73	   * rendering uses the warning variant and SFCC-250 AC4 confirms this never blocks checkout — this
74	   * build's own gate resolved the wording as meaning user-facing feedback, not literally Chakra's
75	   * error severity (the same reconciliation `ZimmInlineMessage`'s own `variant` prop documents —
76	   * `overrides/app/components/ui-kits/atoms/zimmInlineMessage/index.tsx`: "a caller may
77	   * legitimately pass `variant=\"warning\"` for copy whose own requirement text uses the word
78	   * `error`").
79	   */
80	  notifyMaxQuantityReached: () => void;
81	};
82	
83	/**
84	 * Hook — the one surface every cart toast message (success and warning today; whatever SFCC-404's
85	 * real stacking/aggregation rework needs later, including a genuine error) is sent through.
86	 * `emitCartMessage` below is the single call to the underlying toast function — a future rework
87	 * swaps what happens inside this one file, not a hunt across the cart UI for every place that
88	 * fires a toast.
89	 *
90	 * Wraps the **base** `useToast` (`@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/hooks/use-toast`) rather than a
91	 * new `overrides/app/hooks/use-toast.ts` — that path does not exist, and creating it would be an
92	 * unbudgeted Tier 2 change (`protectedFiles.md` would route it to both squads plus tier-2/tier-1
93	 * approvers). See the SFCC-11 plan's own resolved open question 4. This hook is the real "one
94	 * handler" the plan asks for; the base hook underneath it is just the interim renderer SFCC-404
95	 * replaces.
96	 *
97	 * @returns the three named cart-message senders callers actually invoke today. `emitCartMessage`
98	 * itself is intentionally not returned — nothing outside this file needs to send an
99	 * uncatalogued/arbitrary message yet, and a future message is one new named function here, not a
100	 * reason to widen this hook's public surface.
101	 */
102	export const useCartMessages = (): UseCartMessagesReturn => {
103	  // Real return type is implicit `any` (see CartToastFn's own docblock above) — asserted to the
104	  // local narrow type rather than left as `any`, so every call below is checked against the shape
105	  // this file actually depends on.
106	  const toast = useToast() as CartToastFn;
107	  const intl = useIntl();
108	
109	  const emitCartMessage = (title: string, status: CartToastStatus): void => {
110	    // SFCC-404: this is the one real call to the underlying toast function. When SFCC-404's real
111	    // stacking/aggregation rework lands, this is the only line that changes.
112	    toast({ title, status });
113	  };
114	
115	  return {
116	    notifyAddedToWishlist: (productName: string) =>
117	      emitCartMessage(intl.formatMessage(messages.addedToWishlist, { productName }), 'success'),
118	    notifyAlreadyInWishlist: () => emitCartMessage(intl.formatMessage(messages.alreadyInWishlist), 'warning'),
119	    notifyMaxQuantityReached: () => emitCartMessage(intl.formatMessage(messages.maxQuantityReached), 'warning'),
120	  };
121	};

Overall: REWORK (round 2 of the 3-round cap — one more failed round after this stops the loop)

## Consequence first

Right now nobody can open this step's new UI and look at it. All four Storybook stories for `ZimmCartItemActions` (`Default`, `WishlistMoveSuccess`, `AlreadyInWishlist`, `GuestClick`) crash on load with `useMultiSite must be used within MultiSiteProvider` — I didn't infer this from reading the code, I built Storybook, served it, and ran the real stories through `test-storybook --ci` (Playwright-driven, real browser) and watched all four fail. Two consequences follow directly: (1) the visual checkpoint this step owes Marcel cannot happen yet — there's nothing to look at but an error screen — and (2) `qa.yml`'s `storybook-test` CI job is guaranteed to go red the moment this is pushed, because this diff touches `overrides/app/components/**` and `overrides/app/theme/**`, which is exactly what that job's changed-file filter watches.

This is **not** a production bug — shoppers are fine. It's a Storybook-isolation gap only.

## Mechanism

`ZimmLink` (`overrides/app/components/ui-kits/atoms/zimmLink/index.tsx:39`) calls `useSafeHref()` unconditionally, on every render, regardless of whether it's rendering as a link or a button. `useSafeHref()` (`overrides/app/hooks/useSafeHref.ts:18`) calls `useMultiSite()`, which needs a `MultiSiteProvider` somewhere above it in the tree. In the real app this is always true — `MultiSiteProvider` is mounted once, globally, in `_app-config`. In an isolated Storybook render it's only true if the story file supplies its own — which is exactly why five other components in this same codebase that consume `ZimmLink` or `useMultiSite` already carry a local `decorators` block wrapping every story in `<MemoryRouter><MultiSiteProvider ...>`: `zimmLink/index.stories.tsx` itself, plus `footer`, `zimmSizeSelector`, `zimmNavItem`, `zimmSearchInput`. `ZimmCartItemActions` renders two `<ZimmLink>`s and is the one new file that didn't pick up this already-established pattern. The Vitest suite never surfaces this because `index.test.tsx` deliberately mocks `useSafeHref` away (correctly, and with a comment citing the exact same known hazard) — so the unit tests staying green tells you nothing about whether Storybook can render the component.

## Fix (verified, not guessed)

I patched `index.stories.tsx`'s `meta` with the identical decorator `zimmLink/index.stories.tsx` already uses, rebuilt Storybook, and reran `test-storybook` — all four stories went green, including `WishlistMoveSuccess`'s `within(document.body)` toast-text assertion (the exact proof step 4.4's own pass criterion 6 needs). I then reverted my patch — applying it is the Implementer's job, not mine — and confirmed the working tree is back to exactly the two items it started as (`git status` unchanged, `tsc --noEmit` still clean).

**Instruction for `overrides/app/components/ui-kits/molecules/zimmCartItemActions/index.stories.tsx`, `meta` (lines 6-10):** add
```tsx
import React from 'react';
import { MemoryRouter } from 'react-router-dom';
import { MultiSiteProvider } from '@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/contexts';
```
and a `decorators` entry on `meta`, matching `zimmLink/index.stories.tsx:19-31` exactly:
```tsx
decorators: [
  (Story) => (
    <MemoryRouter>
      <MultiSiteProvider
        site={{ id: 'ZimmermannAU', alias: 'au' }}
        locale={{ id: 'en-AU', alias: 'en-AU' }}
        buildUrl={(path: string) => path}
      >
        <Story />
      </MultiSiteProvider>
    </MemoryRouter>
  ),
],
```
This is the whole fix — one file, no logic change, no test change needed (I confirmed all four stories pass unmodified otherwise).

## Per-axis table (most severe first)

| Axis | Verdict | Evidence |
|---|---|---|
| **Design fidelity** | FAIL | Live-reproduced: every story crashes before rendering anything. Nothing to compare to Figma yet — this axis is worse than UNVERIFIED, it's actively broken. |
| **Pass criteria** | FAIL | Criterion 6 explicitly assigns this step "the Storybook `play`/`within(document.body)`/portal-exception proof" as its own job, closing step 4.3's deferred criterion too. That proof does not execute. Criteria 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 7, 8, 9 (React-state half), 10 all checked out on direct re-verification (see below); 11 is correctly deferred to step 4.2's own already-passed test, not re-litigated here. |
| **Correctness** | FAIL | `tsc --noEmit` clean, targeted `npm run test` green (155 tests / 4 files, including `recipeGuards.test.ts` and `theme/index.test.tsx`), `eslint` clean, `npm run audit:tokens` clean (zero new violations — the 9 flagged are all pre-existing, unrelated files). But `qa.yml`'s `storybook-test` job will fail on this diff as it stands — a real, not hypothetical, CI break the Tester's own arc never actually checked for (it re-ran Vitest, not Storybook). |
| **Conformance** | PASS | `var(--zimm-scale-xl)` used correctly for gap, no bare token keys, `Zimm*` namespacing correct, CODEOWNERS routes the new `.css.ts` to both squads (not Tier-2 designer) matching the co-location rule, no data-fetching/SDK hook called directly (`useCartMessages` is the sanctioned stateless-toast-wrapper exception, confirmed by reading it), callback-prop shape matches `product-item`'s established pattern, the `product-item/index.tsx:365` citation is byte-exact. |
| **Completeness** | PASS | Story, both test files, and co-located recipe all present and registered. |
| **Restraint** | PASS | Independently re-confirmed the Orchestrator's 7-file/IN SCOPE finding; `useWishlistAuthDrawer.ts` genuinely untouched; `cartDrawerContainer.tsx` still doesn't exist. Round 1's sessionStorage-namespacing fix is real, not decorative (see falsification below) — no unexplained scope creep either direction. |

## What I tried to falsify

- **Round-1 fix, by mutation:** reverted `usePendingWishlistItem.ts`'s per-`productId` key back to one shared key, reran — 8 of 11 tests failed (all 3 new cross-row-isolation tests plus the ones asserting the exact keyed string), for exactly the collision the fix claims to close. Restored, reran clean (11/11). The round-1 rework is real.
- **The rendered story, live:** built Storybook, served it, ran the actual `play` functions through a real browser via `test-storybook --ci` rather than trusting that well-written `play` code implies a working story. Found the crash above.
- **The prescribed fix, live:** patched the decorator in per the sibling precedent, rebuilt, reran — confirmed all four stories including the toast-portal assertion actually pass — then reverted so I'm not the one editing the diff under review.
- **Cross-checked cited facts rather than trusting the comments that assert them:** `product-item/index.tsx:365` is byte-exact; `link.default`/`text.default` really are the same `grey[900]` primitive; `ZimmLink`'s `sm` size recipe really does carry capitalize/12px/500/hover-distinct/focus-visible-distinct, matching what the plan's inherited-and-annotated claim says.

## What I could not verify

- **Pixel-exact fidelity against the actual Figma node** — I have no Figma access in this environment (the tool list I was given for this task didn't include a Figma call despite the general instructions mentioning one). I checked the numbers algebraically against the token foundations, which is still a source-level check, not the live-measurement-against-Figma standard the plan's own §5.0 sets. This is why the checkpoint below is still owed even after the crash is fixed.
- **A secondary, non-blocking oddity worth a glance at the checkpoint:** `ZimmLink`'s inherited recipe (`zimmLink.css.ts`, unchanged by this diff) computes to a 22px total row height (14px line-height + 2×4px `paddingBlock`), not the 24px this step's own pass criterion 1 text names. That file predates this step and wasn't touched here, so I'm not scoring it as this diff's defect — flagging it only so the checkpoint below doesn't skip past it.
- Step 4.2's own "resume fires after merge and cap" ordering (criterion 11) — correctly deferred to that already-passed step's test; not re-run here.

## Visual checkpoint — owed, and currently blocked until the fix above lands

Once `index.stories.tsx` has the decorator fix, run `npm run storybook` and open:
- `http://localhost:6006/?path=/story/commerce-zimmcartitemactions--default`
- `http://localhost:6006/?path=/story/commerce-zimmcartitemactions--wishlist-move-success`
- `http://localhost:6006/?path=/story/commerce-zimmcartitemactions--already-in-wishlist`
- `http://localhost:6006/?path=/story/commerce-zimmcartitemactions--guest-click`

**Reference:** SFCC-270 AC8 (links live under the stepper) + SFCC-272 AC5-AC8 (wishlist-move behaviours), plan §11.10(4) for the 24px-snapped-from-Figma's-25px gap; the link styling itself is B3's already-approved `ZimmLink` small-size recipe, not new to this step.

**Correct render:** two underlined, capitalized text buttons — "Remove" and "Move to Wishlist" — side by side (not stacked) with a visible ~24px gap, same dark near-black colour on both. Tab to each: a visible focus ring appears that's clearly different from the unfocused state. Hover: colour lightens to mid-grey. No greyed-out/disabled look ever. On `WishlistMoveSuccess`, clicking "Move to Wishlist" produces a toast reading "Cloud 91 Small Clutch added to Wishlist". On `AlreadyInWishlist`, the toast reads "An item in your bag already exists in Wishlist" with a warning look, nothing else changes. On `GuestClick`, clicking produces no toast at all.

**Incorrect render, today:** exactly what I reproduced — a Storybook error boundary reading `useMultiSite must be used within MultiSiteProvider` instead of any of the above, on all four stories.

## Files touched by this diff

- `/Users/marcel.a.n.navarro/Dev/zimmermann-pwa/overrides/app/components/ui-kits/molecules/zimmCartItemActions/index.stories.tsx` — defect, needs the decorator fix above
- `/Users/marcel.a.n.navarro/Dev/zimmermann-pwa/overrides/app/components/ui-kits/molecules/zimmCartItemActions/index.tsx`
- `/Users/marcel.a.n.navarro/Dev/zimmermann-pwa/overrides/app/components/ui-kits/molecules/zimmCartItemActions/usePendingWishlistItem.ts`
- `/Users/marcel.a.n.navarro/Dev/zimmermann-pwa/overrides/app/components/ui-kits/molecules/zimmCartItemActions/usePendingWishlistItem.test.ts`
- `/Users/marcel.a.n.navarro/Dev/zimmermann-pwa/overrides/app/components/ui-kits/molecules/zimmCartItemActions/index.test.tsx`
- `/Users/marcel.a.n.navarro/Dev/zimmermann-pwa/overrides/app/components/ui-kits/molecules/zimmCartItemActions/zimmCartItemActions.css.ts`
- `/Users/marcel.a.n.navarro/Dev/zimmermann-pwa/overrides/app/theme/components/index.ts` (modified — registration only)
- Precedent to copy: `/Users/marcel.a.n.navarro/Dev/zimmermann-pwa/overrides/app/components/ui-kits/atoms/zimmLink/index.stories.tsx`
- Plan: `/Users/marcel.a.n.navarro/Dev/zimmerMANN-skills/.runs/SFCC-11/plan.md` (Step 4.4, `## 5.0 Verification standard`)

## What Marcel is missing

Every gate that ran automatically on this diff (tsc, eslint, vitest, `audit:tokens`) was clean, and would have stayed clean straight into a merged PR — the one thing that would have caught this before CI did was actually opening Storybook, which nobody in this arc did for this specific step. That's the same shape of gap §5.0 was written to close (source-read vs. live-measurement), and it just recurred one layer up: at the "does the story even render" level rather than the "is the rendered pixel value right" level. Worth asking whether the loop should have a standing "launch Storybook for any step that adds or changes a `.stories.tsx`" line, since right now that only happens if someone (Tester, Scorer, or Marcel) thinks to do it by hand.
